clue.text: Lefty in spot — growth delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the words before it are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a spot or blemish is a mark
a cyst is a growth in the body

explanation.surface: A left-winger has a skin blemish, and something growing there has come out.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, mark and cyst run into the sound of the answer; the split of the spelling is only roughly where the two words meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marxist is a follower of Karl Marx's communism, so a lefty in political slang.

clue.text: Tweak food from time to time, providing cracking goodness

indicators.note: cracking a shell opens it up so that something can be put inside

parts.note: my! and goodness! are both mild exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: something done from time to time happens at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters of food
providing that means if

explanation.surface: Adjust your diet now and then, as long as it gives you a good boost.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodness is the exclamation, not virtue or nutrition, which the food setting pushes you towards.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak something is to make a small adjustment, and to modify is to change slightly.

clue.text: Provoked opponents, loading rifle

indicators.note: loading means putting a charge into something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to rifle a place is to ransack or raid it
South and East are opposing players at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Enemies were goaded into action as they loaded a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Rifle is the verb meaning search and steal, not the firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a protest or a laugh is to provoke or stir it up, so raised can mean provoked.

clue.text: Endless hair colourings applied before showering and using conditioner?

indicators.note: with no ends means both the first and the last letters are dropped

parts.note: tints are dyes for hair
it is showering when it is raining

explanation.surface: A haircare routine of dyes followed by a shower and conditioner.
explanation.walkthrough: Conditioner is someone who gets you fit, a trainer, not a hair product; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete working with a fitness coach is in training, preparing body and stamina for competition.

clue.text: Issue latest in correct pronouns

indicators.note: the latest part of a word is the bit that comes last, so its final letter is used

parts.note: last letter of correct
he and me are two pronouns

explanation.surface: A newsy line about the latest debate over using the right pronouns.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a verb or a magazine number, but it is the noun meaning topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic under discussion, as an issue is.

clue.text: Go back with boyfriend, one who wants to stay in?

definitions.text: one who wants to stay in?

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word for go is read from its end

parts.note: to have a go is to have a stab
her man is her boyfriend

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about getting back together with an ex.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman stays 'in' until dismissed, so wants to stay in, unlike a homebody.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket batter's aim is to avoid getting out, so the question mark flags this cryptic description of the player.

clue.text: Prominent features of stag used with sufficient power

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, as a stag is
a law with teeth has enough power to be enforced

explanation.surface: A stag's antlers are prominent and powerful features.
explanation.walkthrough: Prominent is literal: teeth that stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck teeth are upper front teeth that protrude, so they are features of the face that stand out.

clue.text: Tense is wrong in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word is matched by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the tense in a sentence is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like the grammar term but is the adjective; in a non-rhotic British accent the legal word and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means pulled tight, as tense muscles or a stretched rope are.

clue.text: Concrete refuge put up to support partner

parts.note: a mate is a partner

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an animal's lair is its refuge

explanation.surface: A concrete shelter is built to hold up its partner structure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue a piece that supports another sits below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Material can be an adjective meaning physical or tangible, which is the sense of concrete as opposed to abstract.

clue.text: Details of webinar rat established

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters come from within the words that follow

parts.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: A report detailing a rat that appeared in an online seminar.
explanation.walkthrough: Details is a verb here, meaning tells in full.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail events is to recount them fully, which is to tell their story.

clue.text: Tendency of lead character to display cleavage

indicators.note: the lead character of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the following word is kept

parts.note: first letter of display
a cleavage is a split or rift

explanation.surface: A leading actress tends to show off her cleavage.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleavage is used in its sense of a division, not a neckline.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument or of events is their general direction or tendency.

clue.text: Man on board attracted to English woman at last shows face

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: at last points to the very end of the word just before, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of woman
a counter is a playing piece moved on a board game

explanation.surface: A man on a company board falls for an Englishwoman who finally shows her face.
explanation.walkthrough: Man on board means a piece in a board game, not a director; it is attached after the English woman's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter something is to meet or confront it, which is what facing a problem means.

clue.text: Hint for stage, having admitted new independent operators?

parts.words: Hint for stage, having admitted new
parts.note: surface reading: a tip for a play being put on with a newcomer in the cast
setter's reading: the answer read as a clue says liberate the letters of a word for spies, which rearranged give stage with N let in

explanation.surface: Some advice for a theatre production which has taken on a fresh cast member.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works as its own instruction: the first word is an anagram signal and the second its fodder, whose letters reform as STAGE plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Free agents are people, often sports players, not bound by a contract and able to act for themselves.

clue.text: Cockney's satnav announcement on arrival becoming unwanted product

indicators.note: a Cockney accent drops the H, so the phrase is to be heard as such a speaker would say it

parts.note: a satnav announces you are here when you reach the destination

explanation.surface: A London driver's satnav speaks at the end of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner who drops the H, so here becomes 'ere.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the waste compound the body gets rid of in urine, a by-product nobody wants to keep.

clue.text: Stuck-up favourite son, more remote, losing right to be family member

indicators.note: in a down clue, stuck up means set upside down, so these letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: losing a letter means it drops out of the word

parts.note: farther means further away
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A snooty favourite son becomes more distant and loses his rights in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuck-up looks like snobbish, but it turns the favourite and son upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepfather is a mother's husband who is not the child's father, a member of the family by marriage.

clue.text: Appeal judge in charge

parts.note: something with appeal holds our interest
to judge something is to rate it

explanation.surface: A legal appeal goes before the judge presiding over the court.
explanation.walkthrough: In charge reads as describing the judge, but it is the definition: the rate charged on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest rate is the percentage a lender charges, so it is literally what is in the charge for borrowing.

clue.text: Signing up — arranged rent money, pound for year!

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reordered
one thing for another means swapping it in where the other stood

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Joining a scheme means sorting out rent money, paying by the pound rather than by the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound sign letter replaces the year letter at the end of money before the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of officially registering for a course or membership, that is signing up.

clue.text: Recollected happiest commemorations

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered again, so the letters are picked up and put together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People remember the happiest times at memorial occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: Recollected looks like remembered, which fits the memorial theme, but it splits as re-collected.
explanation.definitionFit: Epitaphs are inscriptions on gravestones that honour and remember the dead.

clue.text: In the mood, already hooked up in conversation

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning beforehand

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken aloud, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: people hooked up are paired off

explanation.surface: Someone in the mood for love is already with a partner, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as one word, pre-paired gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared to do something means being willing or ready, so in the mood for it.

clue.text: Worried Spar's restricting lease over joint head of supermarket's concerns

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the mixed letters close round the other piece

parts.note: Spar, a chain of convenience stores, mixed up

indicators.note: turned over means upside down, so the word for lease is read from its end

parts.note: to lease property is to rent it

indicators.note: something worried is shaken about, so the name's letters are mixed

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top letter, so only the start is used

parts.note: first letter of supermarket

explanation.surface: A worried convenience-store chain limits leases on a joint venture concerning a supermarket's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is a chain of small grocery shops in Britain and elsewhere; the 's stands for is, joining it to restricting.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerns in the sense of businesses; partnerships are firms run jointly by partners.

clue.text: Tips from Sainsbury's to include support for ice cream and cakes

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside, so the other piece goes between
the tips of a word are its two ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of Sainsbury's
an ice cream sits in a cone

explanation.surface: Shopping advice from a supermarket: ice cream cones and cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sainsbury's is a large British supermarket chain; tips here are ends, not advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones are small British baked cakes, usually served with jam and cream.

clue.text: Upstanding prime minister regularly spat out

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading from the bottom to the top

parts.note: Robert Peel was a British prime minister

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of spat

explanation.surface: An honourable prime minister keeps getting into spats.
explanation.walkthrough: Upstanding looks like praise for the minister, but it turns the whole thing upside down. Out is used in its sense of unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out cold or out for the count is unconscious, as a sleeper is.

clue.text: Settled, broken by pressure to reject strikes

indicators.note: rejecting something sends it back the way it came, so the word for settled runs backwards
a word broken by another is split open with the other placed in the gap

parts.note: to settle on a perch is to sit, so settled gives sat
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A dispute was resolved, but union pressure has led workers to reject it and strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Strikes is a verb here, meaning hits lightly, not industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap is to strike something lightly, so taps means strikes gently.

clue.text: Advanced cuts squeezing meagre benefits

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: squeezing something is gripping it tightly on both sides, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to lance a boil is to cut it
a meagre amount is a low one

explanation.surface: Advance cuts squeeze the paltry welfare payments people live on.
explanation.walkthrough: The meagre word goes after the first letter of the cutting word.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a regular payment granted to someone, such as a state benefit.

clue.text: Open to entertaining vicar in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: taken as written
Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to have the vicar round now that he has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: Open to looks like willing, but open alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and not concealed.

clue.text: Superheroine finally appearing in Madame Web feature

indicators.note: appearing in places that letter inside the abbreviated title

parts.note: Mme is the abbreviation for Madame

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word before is used

parts.note: last letter of superheroine

explanation.surface: A superheroine at last turns up in the Marvel film Madame Web.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame Web is a 2024 superhero film, but the clue splits it: Madame gives letters and Web begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a joke image or idea that spreads widely online, a typical feature of the internet.

clue.text: Soldier on exercise, Spartan, crushing resistance

indicators.note: crushing something presses it from both sides, so the outer words close in on the letter between

parts.note: PE is physical education
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a Spartan regime is austere or severe

explanation.surface: A soldier on a training exercise meets a tough Spartan who crushes all resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier on looks like a noun phrase about a soldier, but it is the verb meaning keep going; the two outer pieces press the resistance letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom for continuing doggedly in spite of difficulty, which is persevering.

clue.text: Layer cake at the edges thus

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs, so a layer

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of cake

explanation.surface: A layer cake is described by its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: Layer is read as one who lays, not a tier of sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence is a formal adverb meaning for this reason or therefore, which is one sense of thus.

clue.text: Most blue Democrats seen in dubious seats

indicators.note: seen in places the party abbreviation inside the other letters
something dubious is questionable or not straight, so the following letters are set awry

parts.note: D for Democrat, doubled for the plural
seats rearranged

explanation.surface: Losing Democrats are spotted in contested seats, at their most downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue sounds political, the colour of the Conservatives in Britain, but it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means melancholy or sad, so most blue is the superlative, saddest.

clue.text: Improves from cutting drink a little

parts.note: a cutting remark is tart or sharp
to sup is to sip a small amount

explanation.surface: Something gets better if you stop drinking so much.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting looks like reducing, but it is the adjective meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: To tart something up is an informal British idiom for smartening or embellishing it, so improving its look.
